## Background

In this lab we will use AlphaFold to predict protein structure from sequence. 

Multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) are the key inputs to AlphaFold. The neural network uses co-evolution as restraints in folding simulations. Co-evolution is predictive of contacts (i.e. distance restraints). Contacts in proteins are evolutionarily conserved and encoded in an MSA due to co-evolution.

### Making a Contact Map

The following code is used to make a **contact map**. The off-diagonal dots are where the structure folds up. 

```{r}
library(bio3d)
pdb <- read.pdb("4q21")
cm <- cmap(pdb)
plot.cmap(cm)
```

### Physics-Based Approach

The core idea is that you can describe the energy of something based on its shape. Potential functions describe a system's energy as a function of its structure. This approach calculates the potential energy surface that fully describes the energy of a molecular system as a function of its geometry. 

### Knowledge-Based Approach

The basic idea is that we can use probability as a proxy for energy. It uses things we have seen a lot to determine what we might see in similar things. It is limited by what you've seen before. 

AlphaFold built on existing knowledge-based approaches and combined them with physics. For a give sequence, it references input MSA/templates, and then finds the structure with the lowest free energy. 

## HIV-Pr Monomer

We ran AlphaFold2 from [colabfold](https://colab.research.google.com/github/sokrypton/ColabFold/blob/main/AlphaFold2.ipynb#scrollTo=kOblAo-xetgx).

We will:

1. Read all model AF2 files
2. Calculate RMSD between all models
3. Calculate FMSF between all residues of all models
4. Examine AF2 scores pLDDT and PAE
5. Calculate residue conservation scores for all residues


### 1. Read all model AF2 files

We get a zip archive file from colabfold that we have moved to our directory and unzipped.

Assign the unzipped folder to an object:
```{r}
model_dir <- "hivpr_monomer_94b5b/"
```

These are all the pdb files in our folder:
```{r}
pdb_files <- list.files(model_dir, pattern = ".pdb", full.names = T)
```

```{r}
pdbs <- pdbaln(pdb_files, exefile = "msa", fit = T)
```

### 2. Calculate RMSD

```{r}
rd <- rmsd(pdbs)
```

```{r}
library(pheatmap)
colnames(rd) <- paste0("m",1:5)
rownames(rd) <- paste0("m",1:5)
pheatmap(rd)
```

### 3. Calculate RMSF 

```{r}
rf <- rmsf(pdbs$xyz)
plot(rf, type = "h")
```

```{r}
plot(pdbs$b[1,], typ = "l")
points(pdbs$b[2,], typ = "l", col = "red")
points(pdbs$b[3,], typ = "l", col = "blue")
points(pdbs$b[4,], typ = "l", col = "purple")
points(pdbs$b[5,], typ = "l", col = "darkgreen")
```

```{r}
aln_file <- list.files(model_dir, pattern = ".a3m", full.names = T)
```
